title: The 5 Deadliest Volcanic Eruptions Since 1500, Ranked (#1 Killed by Hunger)

scenes.text: The five deadliest eruptions since 1500. The deadliest one didn't kill most people with lava, ash or fire.

scenes.label: Unzen · 15,000 deaths
scenes.text: Number five: Unzen, Japan, 1792. About fifteen thousand people died when part of the volcano collapsed and caused a tsunami.

scenes.label: Nevado del Ruiz · 25,000
scenes.text: Number four: Nevado del Ruiz, Colombia, 1985. Roughly twenty-five thousand died, mostly in mudflows from melted ice.

scenes.label: Mont Pelee · 30,000
scenes.text: Number three: Mont Pelée, Martinique, 1902. About thirty thousand people were killed, mostly by pyroclastic flows.

scenes.label: Krakatau · 36,000
scenes.text: Number two: Krakatau, Indonesia, 1883. Around thirty-six thousand deaths, mainly from the tsunami it caused.

scenes.label: Tambora · 92,000
scenes.text: Number one: Tambora, Indonesia, 1815. About ninety-two thousand deaths, and most were from starvation afterwards.

description:
The five deadliest volcanic eruptions since 1500, ranked by death toll.
Number one, Tambora in 1815, killed about 92,000 people, and most of them died of starvation after the eruption, not in it.
Which one surprised you most?
first_comment: Did you guess starvation for number one? What should we rank next?
